terrain:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production game terrain tilesheet, companion expansion for supplied medieval woodland pixel-art pack.
Input images: first reference is existing environment pack (palette, texture, pixel clusters); second reference is horse sprites (scale and outline). References ONLY; do not reproduce buildings or horses.
Create a NEW flat top-down terrain sheet that works beneath the side-view horses in a 3/4 RPG horse racing game. True crisp pixel art, restrained clustered dithering, dark moss olive grass, warm umber compacted dirt with ochre highlights, occasional muted pebbles, same rustic hand-pixelled woodland aesthetic. Low contrast terrain so horses stay readable. No isometric diamonds, no perspective convergence, no black platformer soil cross-sections.
Exact layout: square 1024x1024 PNG, 4 columns x 4 rows of equal 256x256 square cells, zero gutters, zero outer margins, no labels, no grid lines. Each cell represents a 32x32 pixel tile enlarged exactly 8x using nearest neighbor; crisp square blocks, no smooth shading or antialiasing.
Tile mapping read left to right, top to bottom:
row 1: grass texture A filling entire cell; grass texture B filling entire cell; packed dirt A filling entire cell; packed dirt B filling entire cell.
row 2: top edge of broad dirt area (grass uppermost 1/4, dirt lower 3/4); bottom edge (dirt upper 3/4, grass lower 1/4); left edge (grass leftmost 1/4, dirt right 3/4); right edge (dirt left 3/4, grass rightmost 1/4).
row 3: outer top-left dirt corner with grass on top and left 1/4 margins; outer top-right corner; outer bottom-left corner; outer bottom-right corner.
row 4: inner grass corner at top-left (only upper-left 1/4 square grass and all remaining dirt); inner grass corner top-right; inner grass corner bottom-left; inner grass corner bottom-right.
All dirt in every tile must share identical base palette and matching scale. All grass identical base palette. Straight transition edges connect on adjacent tiles; all material tiles repeat without visible seams. Edge texture is a thin irregular moss fringe within a few pixel blocks of specified boundary. Entire image opaque. No text, horses, props, cast shadows, watermarks, background canvas, frames or gaps. This is usable terrain texture data, not a presentation board.
terrainRepair:
Edit target: attached terrain tilesheet. Keep precisely the current 4x4 layout, the sixteen tile types and their positions, the moss olive / warm umber palette, and low-resolution crisp pixel style.
Fix only tiling defects: remove ALL thin dark grid separator strokes at the three internal horizontal and vertical cell boundaries. Fill those strokes naturally with adjacent grass/dirt pixel texture. Remove any outer border too. This must be edge-to-edge game texture data without lines, gaps, padding or labels. Keep equal square tile cells, exact straight grid alignments at 25%,50%,75% canvas width/height.
Ensure grass and dirt tiles repeat seamlessly: matching outer-edge colors, consistent base value across tiles; use understated smaller stone flecks, no large isolated rocks or flowers touching tile borders. Keep transition positions at 1/4 from their appropriate cell edge, with matching endpoints across corresponding corner/edge tiles. Every cell remains square and tightly fills its own region. No new objects or text. Opaque PNG.
obstacles:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent PNG game obstacle spritesheet; new companion assets for a medieval woodland horse racing game.
Input images: image 1 environment pack is style and palette reference ONLY; image 2 horses is style and pixel-size reference ONLY.
Create exactly 12 separate obstacle sprites in an exact 4-column by 3-row grid. Square canvas 1024x1024, equal rectangular cells 256 wide x 341 high approximately, generous transparent empty margin in every cell, no cell borders. Each individual object fully contained in its cell. No horses or people.
Visual style: carefully hand-drawn low-resolution pixel art matching references, few small flat color ramps, dark brown almost-black crisp outlines, chunky square pixels, warm wood umber and ochre, dark moss green accents, muted grey stone. Represent each sprite as approximately 48x40 logical pixels enlarged using nearest-neighbor. No antialiasing, blur, soft lighting, realistic high resolution woodgrain, vector look, glow, text, labels, decoration board.
Camera: same mild elevated 3/4 RPG view for EVERY object, visible front face and modest top surface, no extreme isometric view. Reference horses will be placed beside them, a horse about 60 logical pixels long and 40 tall. Obstacle heights between 10 and 24 logical pixels, NOT taller than a horse; each barrier simple and narrow enough to jump.
Layout left-to-right, top-to-bottom:
row 1: low single fallen oak log with small visible circular cut end; short rustic two-post single-rail horse jumping hurdle; short rustic two-post double-rail horse jumping hurdle; a compact mound of rounded woodland rocks.
row 2: one low rectangular tied hay bale; two hay bales touching forming a low jump; a low rough timber gate hurdle with diagonal brace; broken low split-rail fence section.
row 3: low moss-covered log; one squat cut tree stump; compact fallen branch obstacle with small twig ends; low rustic stone wall hurdle with 5 irregular blocks.
Every object is isolated on TRUE transparent alpha background; no opaque background, checkerboard illustration, floor tiles, scenery or ground plane. Ground shadows if any are a small hard-edged dark pixel patch directly beneath feet, no blurry shadows. Consistent scale, clean reusable individual game sprites. No text, grid lines, frames or watermarks.
